bantamkit_status.description: Is bantamkit working, and which bantamkit? Returns a short report a person can read in the transcript: `bantamkit Active 🟢` or `bantamkit Degraded 🟠` on the first line, then the version and `build_id` of the code answering, the surfaces it serves, the memory store it is bound to with its index size against its budget, whether the event log is on, and — when degraded — every condition in full with what to do about it. Call it when the user asks whether the server is alive or working, when a bantamkit tool answered oddly and you need to know whether the server is the reason, or when a reply arrived carrying a `bantamkit degraded` footer and you want the rest of it. Every fact is observed at call time from the server's own state; nothing is a heartbeat or a cached verdict. Takes no arguments, writes nothing, and never echoes another call's arguments.

build_identity.description: Which bantamkit build is answering you, readable mid-call. Returns `build_id` — a content fingerprint of the running source and the asset pack it loads — plus the paths it was computed over. Call it when one MCP server name may resolve to more than one install: two endpoints reporting the same `version` are the SAME build only if their `build_id` matches, because a version string moves on release bumps and not on builds. Any fact that cannot be derived comes back as {"unavailable": "<reason>"} and is named in the `unavailable` list — never omitted, never a placeholder that reads as a value. Takes no arguments and reads no state.

memory_compact.description: Free room in persistent memory when `memory_save` was refused for budget. Archives the stalest facts of the writable project store until a fact as large as the biggest one kept will fit, and returns what moved — every archived name with its type and description. Nothing is deleted: archived facts leave the index but stay on disk, and the operator can restore any of them by name. Read-only grants and the profile layer are never touched. Call it after a budget refusal, then retry the save; calling it under budget archives nothing and says so.

reserve.description: Bytes of index headroom to free below the budget. Omit for the default: the size of the largest index line the store holds, capped at half the budget.

memory_recall.description: Search persistent memory. Call BEFORE starting a task that resembles past work. Returns at most k matching facts.

query.description: Words a past-you would have used to describe the fact

memory_save.description: Save ONE durable fact to persistent memory. Use only for facts needed in a future session; never for things derivable from the repo or one-off state.

description.description: One line written to match the FUTURE recall query, not to summarize the body

shiftwork_clock_in.description: Shift-work clock-in: schema-validate the checkpoint file and return the brief for the unit at plan.cursor — {unit, role, invariants, handoff, do_not, files} — to hand to the spawned agent verbatim. Structured refusals, never exceptions: result=escalate when handoff.open_questions is non-empty, result=success when every unit is done or dropped, result=error when the checkpoint fails validation.

shiftwork_clock_out.description: Shift-work clock-out: record a finished unit — set its status, advance plan.cursor, merge handoff_patch, push history_entry onto the 5-entry ring — validating the whole mutated document against the checkpoint schema BEFORE an atomic write (a failure writes nothing and returns result=error). Every success appends one accounting line (unit, role, status, ts, plus your accounting fields, e.g. tokens/duration/model) to <checkpoint>.log.jsonl.

shiftwork_status.description: Shift-work status: read-only progress summary of a checkpoint — units by status, cursor, open-question count, last history entry. Never mutates.

validate_json.description: Validate candidate output text against a JSON Schema. Returns {valid, feedback}; when invalid, feed the feedback back to the model and retry.

bantamkit_read.description: Read a document through a program, never its raw bytes. Call with `path` alone for the manifest: the file's kind, every part (sheet, document, page) with its row count and byte size, and every omission the reader had to make (embedded images, blank rows, unmapped glyphs, unread pages). Then call with `part` (and `offset`) to page rows; row 0 is the header and each page ends with a continuation line naming the next offset or the end of the part. Do not page through a part to find a row: estimate its offset from the row count and jump. Supported kinds: text/markdown/code, docx, xlsx, html, mhtml; pdf on the Python server only. The Node server refuses pdf, doc and rtf until its reader is ported. A refusal names what the reader actually saw in the file rather than the format's error.

path.description: Path to the document, absolute or relative to the server's working directory

part.description: Part name as the manifest reports it (a sheet name, "document", a page); omit to get the manifest

offset.description: Row number of the first row to return; default 0

limit.description: How many rows; default 50, a 3072-byte page ceiling may return fewer
